title: Rabab plucked lute
summary: The rabab, or rubab, is a plucked lute of South and Central Asia, carved from one piece of wood with a skin-covered face. It has melody strings that are plucked with a plectrum, drone strings, and extra strings that ring in sympathy.
howToPlay: Two drone strings sit on the top row, six melody notes in the middle and a strum below.
Notes travel toward a line at the bottom; strike the lane just as a note arrives.
Begin with a drone note and let the melody answer it, then try the strum in six beats.
Finish with the rising phrase, which climbs the whole set of melody notes.
rules: The melody notes follow a minor-like mode of seven degrees; the drone strings sound the root and the fifth below.
A stroke within a hair of the note is perfect, a near one is good, and a missed one scores nothing.
An extra stroke while a song is running costs a few points.
Each song plays twice; three stars need roughly nine notes in ten on time.
One song runs in six beats to the bar, the other two in four.
heritageNote: The rabab is played from Afghanistan across Pakistan and northern India, in courts, villages and concert halls, and it is the national instrument of Afghanistan. Makers carve the body from a single block of mulberry or similar wood and cover it with skin.
